MARKET.head: Cruise lines emerge as experiential sales channel for US wineries
MARKET.summ: From dedicated charters to custom bottlings, wineries are leveraging cruise partnerships to capture engaged audiences and drive long-term sales
takeaways: Cooper's Hawk Winery chartered Virgin Voyages' Valiant Lady for a four-night Caribbean cruise in 2024, integrating its wines across bars and restaurants; the sailing sold out and 30 percent of members signed up for a second charter in February 2027.

Four Feathers Wine Services, a Washington state custom-wine producer, developed a Columbia Valley brut for Holland America's fleet in 2024 that became the most-served adult beverage across the cruise line.

Eleven Eleven Wines, a boutique Napa winery, hosted 60 guests aboard Scenic Eclipse II in a seven-day Mediterranean sailing and achieved a 33 percent conversion rate of non-wine club passengers to repeat customers.

MARKET.head: California and Pacific Northwest grape growers idle vineyards to weather weak market demand
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: A 2025 study of 19 northern Willamette Valley vineyards found idling cut average management costs by 38 percent per acre, with some sites halving expenses.
Vineyard idling, a temporary pause in production lasting one to three years, lets growers avoid bulldozing planted acres while preserving sunk capital and future options.
Richard Hoff at Mercer Ranches in Prosser, Washington has idled about 1,000 of 3,350 acres since 2025; proper maintenance including irrigation and pruning is critical to revive vines later.

MARKET.head: Early harvests reshape wine tourism, shipping, and operating costs worldwide
MARKET.summ: Along with high temperatures, wine regions around the world reported new records for early grape harvests this summer. For some, it was weeks ahead of the traditional fall schedule, for others it was months in advance. In the heart of the Roussillon in France, Domaine Lafage started picking grapes on July 23, something...
takeaways: Domaine Lafage in Roussillon picked grapes July 23, Jean-Marc Lafage's earliest date ever; California's Central Coast harvested six to eight weeks early, the earliest Kevin Merrill has seen in 27 years.

Aaron Jackson's Aaron Wines tasting room in Paso Robles saw July visitation plummet as heat discouraged wine tourism; direct-to-consumer shipping blackout periods lengthened as safe shipping windows narrowed across the year.

Winemakers face new costs: higher electricity for early-harvest refrigeration during peak-price summer months, delayed cash flow when shipping is delayed until fall, and damage to bottle labels in extreme heat requiring costly reprints.

MARKET.head: Southern Glazer's pays $12.5M to settle DOJ bribery investigation
MARKET.summ: On Thursday, alcohol distributor Southern Glazer’s announced that it reached a resolution with the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Alcohol and Tobacco Trade Bureau (TTB) in a longstanding investigation related to improper payments and bribery. In the deal, Southern agreed to pay $12.5 million.
takeaways: Southern Glazer's, the US alcohol distributor, reached a non-prosecution agreement with the DOJ and TTB on Thursday, paying $12.5 million to resolve a bribery investigation.

Former employees allegedly distributed cash, gift cards, luxury goods, golf trips, flights and resort bookings to California retailers from 2016 to 2024 to secure better shelf placement and other benefits.

Southern Glazer's agreed to strengthen compliance controls and fulfil undisclosed obligations over two years; the company claims it has already increased TTB compliance staff and implemented proactive auditing.

MARKET.head: US tariff lift and India trade deal reshape Scotch whisky market in 2026
MARKET.summ: Is it possible that 2026 could eventually be looked back on as the make-or-break year for Scotch whisky? In July, the U.S. finally lifted its 15 month tariff on Scotch, one that had contributed to a 15 percent decline in exports to this country, one of Scotland’s biggest international markets.
takeaways: US lifted its 15-month tariff on Scotch in July 2026, after the levy contributed to 15 percent export decline to America, Scotland's largest market.
UK-India free trade agreement signed same month may open the world's largest whisky market to more affordable Scotch imports.
Post-pandemic oversupply persists; major distilleries including Diageo and Brown-Forman remain paused, while premiumization fatigue pushes focus to sub-$100 age-stated bottles.

SCIENCE.head: Wildfires destroy 200 hectares in Sierra de Gredos wine region
SCIENCE.summ: The ethereal Garnachas of Sierra de Gredos have brought new recognition to this Spanish winemaking region, but after wildfires recently swept through the region, can the momentum continue?
takeaways: Fires between July 22 and 26 destroyed 77,000 hectares across Ávila and Madrid provinces; approximately 200 hectares of vineyards in Cebreros DO suffered fire, smoke, or both damage.
Multiple producers including Bodegas Bernabeleva and Bodega El Reventón reported destroyed vineyard parcels, infrastructure damage, and uncertainty over grape viability for the vintage.

Comando G's Las Iruelas single-vineyard parcel in Cebreros suffered heavy smoke exposure, likely making the wine unviable; other Comando G sites in Villanueva, Navatalgordo, Cadalso de los Vidrios, and Rozas de Puerto Real were spared.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: The purpose of any honest writing competition can only be to support and encourage the craft and industry of writing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Pluralism Of Wine Writing
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Einstein was there before us. As he famously put it, I know not with what technologies the third 67 Pall Mall awards were fought, but the fourth will be fought with quills and inkwells. Perhaps entrants will be invited to nearby Westminster school and asked to produce their submissions in real time.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A winning entry in the Pall Mall awards' short-form writing competition faced allegations of AI use, with organizers stating the work is "not 100% AI-generated.".
Tim Atkin argues wine writing encompasses diverse forms, journalism, criticism, and travelogue, whose definitions remain fluid and whose quality varies widely across styles.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Video: Vintage time at Hundred Hills, making the Rosé de Saignée cuvée
NEWSLETTERS.summ: It’s the penultimate day of harvest at Oxfordshire winery Hundred Hills. They are picking Pinot Noir for the famed Rosé
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Hundred Hills winery in Oxfordshire produces Rosé de Saignée by macerating destemmed Pinot Noir on skins, then pressing to barrel when colour reaches desired level.
The winery was harvesting Pinot Noir on the penultimate day of their 2026 vintage harvest at the time of filming.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Heading Out
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Preparing to jump to Italy next week, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker travels to Piemonte next week for a press tour of Roero, tasting wines alongside handmade cheese, truffle, hazelnut, and honey.
Press tours are funded by regional consortiums, marketing agencies, and EU subsidies, positioning journalists as the product acquired to generate favorable coverage.
Sarah Marsh MW cautioned at the Old Vine Conference that not all old vines are superior; many carry viruses and health issues affecting resilience to climate extremes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Myths of The Douro
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If you thought Portugal’s most famous wine region was just heat, heft and port, read on
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Global port sales have declined 25% over the last two decades, while the Douro now produces as much table wine as port, making unfortified wine the region's economic mainstay.
The Douro's vineyard grading system rewards sites suited to port production with high sugar, colour and tannin, creating a reputation for heavy wines that doesn't reflect the region's full potential.

New-generation winemakers like Rita Marques, Luis Seabra, and Pedro Coelho are producing lighter, high-altitude Douro wines with acidity and classical structure, challenging the port-legacy style of earlier table wine producers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a separate Wine & Spirits subsection within its Rising and Top lists, splitting it from the larger Food & Drink category to improve discovery.
Miquel Hudin updated the Wine Substack List (WineStack), now requiring paid subscriptions and human-written text only, removing "Thirst Behavior" by Bodhi Landa for AI-generated content.
Matthew Jukes, a traditional wine media writer, passed away last month.
